_about: Single source of truth for Act 1 (500 BC to 1836). Both build_act1.py (Blender scene/animation) and overlay.py (year counter, population counter, captions) read this file. Times are in seconds from the start of the act. 'year_at' keys define the year counter (linear between keys). Every caption fact comes from data/events.json / war_sequences.json.
title: Before the City

date_label.note: during the lighthouse attack show day precision

population_note: 800 is the low end of the Tequesta estimate (800-10,000 across their territory); 180 is the 1743 Spanish count; 20 and 80 are illustrative (settlers; plantation with about 60 enslaved people). Show a small 'est.' next to the counter before 1743.

caption.title: THE TEQUESTA
caption.sub: Fishers of the bay. At the river mouth they cut a circle into the rock

beats.scene: Untouched bay at golden hour. Mangroves, pine ridge, sawgrass to the west. Smoke from cooking fires at the river mouth.

caption.title: THE MIAMI CIRCLE
caption.sub: 600 post holes in a 38-foot ring. Nothing like it survives anywhere else in the eastern US

beats.scene: Slow push-in to the river mouth. Village grows on both banks; canoes crisscross the bay; the circle of posts at Brickell Point.

caption.title: SAILS
caption.sub: 1513: Ponce de Leon enters the bay and calls it Chequescha

beats.scene: Two Spanish ships come in north of Key Biscayne (no Government Cut yet), cruise past, leave. Canoes gather at the shore to watch.

caption.title: THE MISSION
caption.sub: 30 soldiers and a Jesuit brother build a stockade. He starts teaching the children

beats.scene: 1566: ships anchor off the mouth; a cross goes up. 1567: timber stockade rises beside the village.

caption.title: THE VILLAGE BURNS
caption.sub: Soldiers kill the chief's uncle. The Tequesta burn their own homes and vanish into the Everglades

beats.scene: Huts catch fire one after another (spreading, not all at once). A line of canoes paddles west up the river. Smoke drifts over the bay.

caption.title: RETREAT
caption.sub: They come back and attack the garrison. The soldiers sail for St. Augustine. By 1570 the mission is gone

beats.scene: Ship leaves north; empty stockade; burned patches.
Fast time: village partly rebuilds, fewer huts than before.

caption.title: RAIDERS FROM THE NORTH
caption.sub: Carolina slavers and their Yamasee allies empty Florida. In 1710 a ship takes 280 people to Cuba; nearly 200 die

beats.scene: Huts disappear in clusters; a single Spanish ship leaves south. Sober tone, no figures fighting.

caption.title: THE LAST MISSION
caption.sub: 1743: two Jesuits find 180 people left, half of them children. They stay a few months

beats.scene: Small stockade on the water's edge; a handful of huts.

caption.title: GONE
caption.sub: 1763: Florida becomes British. The last people of the bay sail for Cuba

beats.scene: Canoes to a ship offshore; empty village; population counter reaches 0. Vegetation creeps over the site.

caption.title: SQUATTERS
caption.sub: Bahamian wreckers and farmers drift in. By 1800 a few families live on the bay

beats.scene: Fast time, empty landscape; a few palm-thatch shacks appear on the shore.

caption.title: A LIGHT FOR THE REEF
caption.sub: 1825: a 65-foot brick lighthouse on Cape Florida

beats.scene: Camera swings south; the white tower rises course by course; the beam comes on at dusk.

caption.title: THE PLANTATION
caption.sub: 1830: Richard Fitzpatrick clears the north bank. About 60 enslaved people grow sugar cane and citrus

beats.scene: Rectangular fields cut into the hammock on the north bank; a main house and rows of cabins.

caption.title: THE 1835 HURRICANE
caption.sub: Key Biscayne goes under three feet of water

beats.scene: Dark sky, the water plane rises over the island, then drains.

caption.title: WAR
caption.sub: January 1836: the Second Seminole War begins. The plantation is abandoned

beats.scene: Boats leave the river mouth; fields go quiet.

caption.title: THE LIGHTHOUSE
caption.sub: 23 July 1836, about 4 p.m.: Seminole warriors land on Cape Florida

beats.scene: Afternoon light. A canoe/sloop grounds on the beach; small figures fan out around the tower. Musket smoke puffs.

caption.title: FIRE
caption.sub: The door burns. Bullets pierce the oil tanks and 225 gallons of lamp oil catch fire

beats.scene: Fire at the tower base; glow climbing inside the windows; keeper's house looted.

caption.title: THE LAST STAND
caption.sub: Keeper John Thompson and Aaron Carter climb to the top and cut away the stairs. Carter is killed

beats.scene: Sun sets fast (time dilation). Two tiny figures at the lantern gallery; flames below.

caption.title: THE POWDER KEG
caption.sub: Thompson throws a keg of gunpowder down the burning tower. It explodes; the tower stands

beats.scene: Night. Bright flash inside the tower, sparks out of the windows; raiders leave in the dark; keeper's house burning.

caption.title: RESCUE
caption.sub: The Navy schooner Motto heard the blast 12 miles away. Next day they fire a line up to him on a ramrod

beats.scene: Dawn. Schooner anchors off the point; a rowboat lands; smoke still rising.

caption.title: FORT DALLAS
caption.sub: The Navy builds blockhouses at the mouth of the Miami River

beats.scene: Back at the river mouth: blockhouses and a flag on the abandoned plantation; a schooner in the bay. End of Act 1.

shots._about: Camera keys. target = look-at point (lat, lon); dist_m = distance from target; elev_deg = camera elevation angle; az_deg = direction the camera sits FROM the target (0 = north, 90 = east). Shots blend over 'blend_s'.
